meta.method: GA4 BOOKINGS ARE ON THE CREATE PATH FROM THIS WEEK. Boundary date 12 October 2026. Bookings = eventCount where eventName EXACTLY 'sevenrooms_booking_complete' AND pagePath does not match 'modify|manage|prearrival' by PARTIAL_REGEXP, implemented as an andGroup with a notExpression. That keeps /explore/aquakyotoparis/reservations/create/checkout/ plus the /reservations/aquakyotoparis landing route and drops /explore/aquakyotoparis/reservations/modify/checkout/. All four TY weeks and all four LY weeks in the trends payload were rebuilt on this basis, so both sides of every comparison are like for like. GA4 weekly users are deduplicated (one call per Mon-Sun week, no date dimension, never summed from daily rows). Google bookings use metrics.all_conversions filtered to conversion action 'Aqua Kyoto Paris (web) sevenrooms_booking_complete'; raw metrics.conversions is never used. Campaign spend and campaign booking conversions were pulled as two separate GAQL queries because segments.conversion_action_name cannot be selected alongside cost_micros. Meta bookings = action_type 'offsite_conversion.fb_pixel_custom' (the Paris exception). Meta used time_increment=7 from a Monday start, one call per account per year. trend8/funnel spend and bookings = Meta plus Google combined. funnel.landing = GA4 Paid Search plus Paid Social sessions. Campaign table ordered by spend descending across both platforms; the wow arrow is the spend direction against the prior week.

problems: HEADLINE. GA4 bookings 189 on the create path, down 32.5 percent on W36's 280 and down 32.7 percent on the year-ago 281. Users 3,829, down 17.3 percent WoW. Conversion rate 4.94 percent against 6.05 percent last week and 3.44 percent a year ago. Paris has no target, so WoW and YoY are the only comparisons.

CREATE-PATH BOUNDARY APPLIED THIS WEEK, PARIS NOW CHECKED. Amendment share at Paris: W37 2026 is 12 of 201 events, 6.0 percent; the year-ago week 13 to 19 Oct 2025 is 22 of 303, 7.3 percent. Across the four TY weeks it is 64 of 1,121 (5.7 percent) and across the four LY weeks 71 of 982 (7.2 percent). The two years were therefore about 1.5 points apart, far less than the 9 points found in London Oct 2025, so restating moves the Paris YoY only from -33.7 percent (all paths) to -32.7 percent (create path). Both sides of every comparison in this week's payloads are on the create path. Published Paris weeks up to and including w2026-10-05 remain on the old all-paths basis and have not been restated in place.

THE ONE THING THAT NEEDS ATTENTION. The booking fall is not a tracking break and it is not the widget. Create-path bookings by day ran 28, 34, 34, 44 Monday to Thursday then 22, 16, 10 Friday to Sunday, against 43, 42, 42 on the same three days of W36. Sessions that reached the reservation flow were 273, 267, 278, 342 Monday to Thursday then 185, 133, 105 Friday to Sunday, against 332, 412, 315 a week earlier. Conversion from flow session to booking held between 9.5 and 12.9 percent every day of the week, in line with the 10.2 to 13.3 percent of W36. So the step that broke is entry into the booking flow: flow sessions as a share of site sessions were 37.6, 36.3, 37.1 and 41.4 percent Monday to Thursday and 26.1, 23.3 and 19.8 percent Friday to Sunday, against 41.9, 42.5 and 38.7 percent the previous Friday to Sunday. Worth checking whether a site, CTA or availability change landed on or around Friday 16 October.

The drop is in unpaid traffic. Organic Search sessions 1,513 from 2,152, down 29.7 percent, with create-path bookings 63 from 119. Direct 858 from 1,442, down 40.5 percent, with bookings 52 from 87. Paid Search rose to 956 from 872 and Paid Social was flat at 794 from 818. Paid delivery therefore held while organic and direct fell, which is the opposite shape to a budget-driven week.

GA4 engagement rate 72.2 percent and average session duration 310 seconds this week, against a restated 67.0 percent and 164 seconds for W36. Average session duration nearly doubling in a week that bookings fell a third is not a demand signal; treat both as provisional under the documented 6 to 9 point restatement rule and re-read next run.

Meta improved sharply and Google deteriorated. Meta spent 1,661.50 for 54 fb_pixel_custom bookings, a 30.77 CPA, its best of the eight weeks shown, against 1,675.19 for 39 at 42.95 in W36. Google spent 1,611.33 for 43.0 booking conversions, a 37.47 CPA, its worst of the eight weeks, against 1,547.82 for 55.0 at 28.14. Note the divergence: Meta bookings rose 38 percent in the same week GA4 bookings fell 33 percent.

Google YoY is the weakest line in the report. The same week last year, 13 to 19 Oct 2025, returned 64.0 booking conversions for 989.67 at a 15.46 CPA. Google is now paying 2.4 times as much per booking as it did a year ago on 63 percent more spend for 33 percent fewer bookings.

Meta bookings definition on this account: offsite_conversion.fb_pixel_custom reads 54 this week; strict schedule_total reads 0, so it does not even appear in the conversions block. The fb_pixel_custom total is used, same as all prior Paris weeks. Strict schedule_total would make Meta CPA undefined.

LY Meta CPA is not a usable comparator. 13 to 19 Oct 2025 spent 1,853.18 for 2 fb_pixel_custom bookings, a 926.59 CPA, because the Paris Meta pixel logged almost nothing through launch. The Meta CPA card will show a large favourable YoY badge that means nothing. Read the Meta CPA line against the TY weeks only.
